podcast.title: Murder at Chelsea Hotel (October 12, 1978)
podcast.body: Nancy Spungen, girlfriend of Sid Vicious, was found dead from a single stab wound to her stomach in room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel in New York on October 12, 1978. Nancy had a troubled life, diagnosed with schizophrenia at 15 and supporting herself through prostitution from age 17 before becoming a groupie to bands like The Ramones, New York Dolls, and Aerosmith. She became inseparable from Sid Vicious for 19 months, and they both were heroin and Tuinal addicts. On the night of October 11, 1978, several people visited their room, and Sid allegedly took up to 52 Tuinal tablets, completely incapacitating him. At around 2:30 am on October 12th, Nancy asked Rockets Redglare, their drug connection and Sid's bodyguard, for Dilaudid. Later, around 7:30 am, female moans were heard, and at 10 am, Sid called the front desk. Nancy was found stabbed and bleeding to death, in a weird angle under the bathroom sink. Sid initially confessed but was likely too incapacitated. The theory later emerged that Rockets Redglare, who died in 2007, was the murderer, allegedly stabbing Nancy with Sid's Bowie knife during an argument over stolen cash, a confession he reportedly made while drinking at CBGB. "Nancy Spungin, girlfriend of ex-sex Bristol Sidvicious, at the Chelsea Hotel on October 12, 1978."

podcast.title: Unsolved Mystery - Suspects and Theories
podcast.body: While Sid Vicious was charged with her murder, many dispute his guilt, suggesting a New York actor and drug dealer named Rockets Red Glare (Michael Mora) as a primary alternative suspect. A theory posits that Rockets brought drugs to the hotel around 1:30 AM on October 12, stayed until 5 AM while Sid was unconscious, stole a large amount of money (up to $20,000), and then murdered Nancy, whose autopsy indicated she died between 5 and 9 AM. "The favorite suspect by most is a New York actor and drug dealer who went by the name Rockets Red Glare. He was a hangar on with Sid and Nancy, often supplying them with drugs. At around 1.30 in the morning of October the 12th, Nancy called Rockets and asked him to bring some drugs. He arrived somewhere after 3 and stayed until about 5. Remember Sid is apparently completely unconscious at this point. The autopsy on Nancy suggested that she died between 5 and 9 am. The police report also says that a large amount of money was missing from the room, maybe as much as $20,000. Rockets was spotted at the hotel at around 4. There were two or three people who confirmed seeing him."

xref.title: Death by Heroin Overdose (February 2, 1979)
xref.body: Sid Vicious died at 21 years old from a heroin overdose. He was out on bail awaiting trial for the murder of his girlfriend Nancy Spungen. After 55 days in Riker's Island prison, a completely detoxed Sid was released on February 1, 1979, and celebrated his freedom with his mom Beverly, new girlfriend Michelle Robinson, and friends at Michelle's apartment at 63 Bank Street in New York. His mom called over English photographer and dealer Peter Codic to deliver heroin for him. Sid took a "taste" as a dessert, but due to his detoxed state, his body was super vulnerable to the 99% pure heroin, causing him to overdose. They revived him and put him to bed, which was a fatal move as he should have been kept awake until the drug left his system. The next morning, February 2, he was found stone-cold dead in bed next to Michelle. "Apparently the heroin he took the night before was 99% pure. And since he had detoxed, his body was super vulnerable."

xref.title: Sid Vicious Ashes Allegedly Spilled at Heathrow Terminal 4 (February 1979)
xref.body: After Sid Vicious's death on February 2, 1979 (heroin overdose while awaiting trial for the murder of Nancy Spungen), his mother Anne Beverly had him cremated. Two weeks later, allegedly drunk while returning to London through Heathrow Airport, she tripped, fell, and spilled Sid's ashes in the terminal — some reportedly embedded in the carpet and sucked into the ventilation system. Rumor holds that Sid Dust still circulates through Terminal 4. However, those with knowledge say this is not what happened: what is confirmed is that before returning to England, Anne took his ashes to Nancy Spungen's grave in Philadelphia and spread them there. What is also confirmed is that New York police tipped off London police, who raided Anne's Notting Hill home, found drugs, and arrested her. Anne Beverly died on September 6, 1996, after carefully putting her affairs in order and then consuming a large quantity of painkillers, tranquilizers, and alcohol. "Rumor has it that Sid Dust still circulates throughout terminal four."
